claims.claim: Tikal had no water other than rainwater, stored in ten reservoirs
claims.quote: Tikal had no water other than what was collected from rainwater and stored in ten reservoirs.

claims.claim: Rainwater was caught in the plazas
claims.quote: The main plazas were surfaced with stucco and laid at a gradient that channelled rainfall into a system of canals that fed the reservoirs.

claims.claim: Tikal was a city of thousands of inhabitants
claims.quote: Population estimates for Tikal vary from 10,000 to as high as 90,000 inhabitants.

claims.claim: Card 1 image is the Great Plaza at Tikal, photographed by Gary Todd in 2002, CC0
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Tikal Great Plaza (9791228163).jpg ... Date: 2002-04-04 18:53 ... Author: Gary Todd ... Licence: CC0

claims.claim: The last inhabitants left after the 10th or 11th century
claims.quote: Even these final inhabitants abandoned the city in the 10th or 11th centuries and the rainforest claimed the ruins for the next thousand years.

claims.claim: Temples over 70 metres tall stood in the rainforest
claims.quote: The architecture of the ancient city is built from limestone and includes the remains of temples that tower over 70 meters (230 ft) high

claims.claim: The forest held the site for a thousand years
claims.quote: the rainforest claimed the ruins for the next thousand years

claims.claim: Card 2 image shows a Tikal temple rising above the forest canopy (Gary Todd, 2002, CC0)
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Tikal (10515143573).jpg ... Date: 2002-04-04 22:32 ... Author: Gary Todd

claims.claim: Cinnabar, a mercury-bearing pigment, coated monuments and facades at Tikal
claims.quote: This toxicity resulted primarily from the widespread ceremonial application of cinnabar-based pigments on monumental architecture and stelae throughout the Classic Period.

claims.claim: Rain washed the cinnabar into the central reservoirs, poisoning them
claims.quote: Rainwater runoff continuously leached these toxic mineral compounds from plastered facades directly into the central urban catchment basins, rendering the immediate water supply biohazardous

claims.claim: Card 3 image shows a carved mask at Tikal
claims.quote: maskcarving.jpg — image shows a large carved stone/stucco relief of a mask-like face with modelled snout and scroll elements, beside plastered steps

claims.claim: Sapodilla wood lintels span doorways at Tikal
claims.quote: At Tikal, beams of sapodilla wood were placed as lintels spanning the inner doorways of temples.

claims.claim: They are the most elaborately carved wooden lintels to survive in the Maya region
claims.quote: These are the most elaborately carved wooden lintels to have survived anywhere in the Maya region.

claims.claim: Card 4 image shows wooden lintels in Group G, dated to the 8th century
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Tikal Group G Wood Lintels, 8th Century (9791228114).jpg

claims.claim: Wooden beams are still in place spanning a doorway in the photograph
claims.quote: lintel.jpg — image shows multiple weathered wooden beams spanning a doorway opening, with green foliage visible through the gap below

claims.claim: Jasaw Chan K'awiil II raised a stela in the Great Plaza in 869
claims.quote: as evidenced by a stela erected in the Great Plaza by Jasaw Chan Kʼawiil II in 869

claims.claim: Nothing was carved/erected at Tikal after that monument
claims.quote: This was the last monument erected at Tikal before the city finally fell into silence.

claims.claim: Card 5 image is 'The Serpent Bird' by A. P. Maudslay, 1899, public domain
claims.quote: Archive title: File:A glimpse of Guatemala - The Serpent Bird, Tikál.png ... Date: 1899 ... Author: Alfred Percival Maudslay ... Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: The most likely cause of collapse was overpopulation and agrarian failure
claims.quote: The most likely cause of collapse at Tikal is overpopulation and agrarian failure.

claims.claim: Recent reservoir research points instead to meteorological drought
claims.quote: new research regarding paleoenvironmental proxies from the Tikal reservoir system suggests that a meteorological drought may have led to the abandonment of Tikal

claims.claim: Squatters lived in the royal palaces before the end
claims.quote: its royal palaces were occupied by squatters and simple thatched dwellings were being erected in the city's ceremonial plazas

claims.claim: Card 6 image is an 1882 photograph of Tikal by Alfred Percival Maudslay, public domain
claims.quote: Archive title: File:Tikal1882.jpeg ... Date: 1882 ... Author: Alfred Percival Maudslay ... Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: Tikal lies in the Petén rainforest of Guatemala
claims.quote: it is located in the archaeological region of the Petén Basin in what is now the Petén Department in northern Guatemala

claims.claim: Tikal was one of the largest cities in the Americas
claims.quote: It was one of the largest of the Classic period Maya cities and was one of the largest cities in the Americas.

claims.claim: Population estimates run from 10,000 to 90,000 in the city core
claims.quote: Population estimates for Tikal vary from 10,000 to as high as 90,000 inhabitants.

claims.claim: Far higher population figures are given for the hinterland
claims.quote: In a region within a 25 kilometers (16 mi) radius of the site core and including some satellite sites, peak population is estimated at 425,000

claims.claim: The city covered more than 16 square kilometres and had about 3,000 mapped structures
claims.quote: The city has been completely mapped and covered an area greater than 16 square kilometers (6.2 sq mi) that included about 3,000 structures.

claims.claim: Temple IV is the tallest pyramid and rises 70 metres
claims.quote: Temple IV is the tallest temple-pyramid at Tikal, measuring 70 meters (230 ft) from the plaza floor level to the top of its roof comb.

claims.claim: The city had no rivers, springs or wells
claims.quote: Tikal had no water other than what was collected from rainwater and stored in ten reservoirs.

claims.claim: Rainwater was channelled through canals into ten reservoirs from stucco-surfaced plazas
claims.quote: The main plazas were surfaced with stucco and laid at a gradient that channelled rainfall into a system of canals that fed the reservoirs.

claims.claim: The Corriental reservoir filtered drinking water through layers of zeolite minerals and quartz sand
claims.quote: the drinking water in the Corriental reservoir was filtered through layers of Clinoptilolite and Mordenite zeolites, in addition to coarse to very coarse sand-sized quartz crystals

claims.claim: Sediment cores from the Temple and Palace reservoirs show severe mercury contamination
claims.quote: geochemical analyses of sediment cores from the Temple and Palace reservoirs have revealed severe historical mercury contamination

claims.claim: Between 830 and 950 Tikal lost most of its population
claims.quote: Tikal and its immediate surroundings seem to have lost most of their population between 830 and 950

claims.claim: Old tombs were dug open for jade
claims.quote: with the tombs of the North Acropolis being explored for jade and the easier-to-find tombs were looted

claims.claim: Some archaeologists think the population figures are far too high
claims.quote: However, some archaeologists, such as David Webster, believe these figures to be far too high.

claims.claim: Local people never forgot the site and guided Guatemalan expeditions to the ruins in the 1850s
claims.quote: It seems that local people never forgot about Tikal and they guided Guatemalan expeditions to the ruins in the 1850s.
